To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the full-length pro-Matrix Metalloproteinase-8 (MMP-8) has an elongated structure and its unique O-glycosylation domain (OG) is unstructured and flexible.
the multidomain structure and flexibility of pro-matrix metal-loproteinase-9 are essential for its activity and regulation.

the proline-rich, O-glycosylation-rich, and flexible domain of full-length pro-gelatinase B (pro-MMP-9) plays a key role in the regulation of its activity and in the recognition of its substrates and receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the structural basis of the MMP-9 function, which may help to develop more efficient and specific therapeutic approaches.
the structural organization of full-length pro- MMP-9 and provides a molecular basis for its function.
the structure and dynamics of full-length pro- MMP-9, which will be useful for the rational design of selective and effective MMP-9 inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pro-MMP- 9 structure is highly flexible with two globular domains, a long linker region, and a flexible and highly glycosylated domain.
the OG domain of full-length MMP-9 is flexible and may be an important target for the design and discovery of selective MMP-9 inhibitors.
the OG domain is a key element in the structural flexibility and function of pro-MMP-8 and pro-MMP-13, as well as in the structure and activity of pro-MMP9.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we report the structure of full-length proMMP-9 and show the importance of the OG-domain in the regulation and function of the protein.
the structure of pro-MMP- 9 has been solved, and it is now possible to design selective regulators of MMP-9.

we have provided a structural model for full-length pro-Matrix Metalloprotease-9, a multidomain zinc endopetidase, and demonstrated that its O-Glycan rich domain is flexible and may be an additional target for design of regulators.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prodomain of MMP-9 is a highly flexible and dynamic domain.
the structure of pro-MMP-2/3/9 can be described in terms of two globular domains connected via a long, flexible, and O-glycosated linker.
the OG domain in pro-MMP-2 and pro-MMP-13 has a similar molecular character and may play a similar role in the regulation and activity of these two other members of the gelatinase family.
